name: msc-generator
desc: Draws signalling charts from textual description
why: Text description becomes signalling charts, a small domain language with a satisfying transform.

brief.what_it_is: msc-generator is a tool that draws signalling charts (message sequence charts), block diagrams and graphs from a text description. The GitLab project page describes it as drawing 'signalling charts, block diagrams and graphs from text input'. The brief's scout notes call it a small domain language. I could not read the README body, so I cannot confirm the input syntax or the output formats. The executable it installs is msc-gen.
brief.why_it_exists: The project page gives no problem statement or motivation beyond the one-line description. I found no author framing in the text I could read.
brief.install_notes: I did not see install steps. The brew formula lists msc-gen as the executable. The project has a GUI tag, so a graphical front end may exist, but I could not confirm it.
brief.standout: The scout notes describe it as a small text domain language with a satisfying text-to-chart transform. I could not verify this from the README, so treat it as unconfirmed until a writer checks the README directly.
brief.status: Unknown. The GitLab page shows the project was created on November 09, 2021. It shows no last-release or last-commit date, and the README body did not load, so I cannot judge whether it is maintained.
brief.caveats: The README body did not render. The README fetch returned only page chrome, and the docs site at msc-generator.gitlab.io returned HTTP 403. Nothing I say about syntax, commands or features is verified. The license shown on the page is GNU AGPLv3.
